deep.reconstruction:
The page has no previous page and is a dense scratch sheet. It is entirely about composing linear substitutions in four variables that are built from pairs of binary (2x2) substitutions. ∂ is Riemann's letter d.

(A) Top block (only partly recoverable). It is a 4-column array of products of the ratios c/a, ∂/b, c1/a1, ∂1/b1, c2/a2, ∂2/b2. Each entry is a product of one factor from each of two or three substitutions (a,b,c,∂), (a1,b1,c1,∂1), (a2,b2,c2,∂2), normalised by the leading coefficients. Examples: 1; -(c2/a2)(∂1/b); -(c1/a1)(∂1/b1) + (c∂/ab)(c2/a2)(∂2/b2); (c/a)(c2/a2)(∂1/b1); (∂/b)(c1/a1)(∂2/b2). The right-hand notes a1b1·ab·a2b2, a1a2·ab and b1b2·ab are the common denominators needed to clear these fractions. Further down, 'ab - c∂, b c, a∂' lists the entries and determinant of a binary substitution. In my reading this block is a first attempt to multiply out a product of substitutions written in normalised form. The exact matrix cannot be fixed with certainty.

(B) 4x4 substitutions. The substitution
M = [[α,0,0,β],[0,-γ,-δ,0],[γ,0,0,δ],[0,α,β,0]]
is written twice; a companion matrix in α1,β1,γ1,δ1 is struck out. Rows 1 and 3 act on (x1,x4) through A = [[α,β],[γ,δ]]. Rows 2 and 4 act on (x2,x3) through [[-γ,-δ],[α,β]]. Hence (my addition) det M = -(αδ-βγ)^2.

Riemann then composes an inner substitution
z1 = α1x1+β1x4, z2 = -β1x2+α1x3, z3 = γ1x1+δ1x4, z4 = ±(δ1x2-γ1x3)
with an outer one
αz1+βz2, -γz3+δz4, γz1+δz2, αz3+βz4.
These two compositions are written out in two variants, upper right and lower right. The coefficient table of the composite is (rows = new variables, columns = x1..x4):
- row 1: αα1, -ββ1, βα1, αβ1
- row 2: -γγ1, δδ1, -δγ1, -γδ1
- row 3: γα1, -δβ1, δα1, γβ1
- row 4: αγ1, -βδ1, βγ1, αδ1

Every entry is a product of one entry of A with one entry of B = [[α1,β1],[γ1,δ1]]. Up to the same signed permutation of rows and columns, this is the Kronecker product A⊗B: index order (11),(22),(21),(12), with the second index negated. Call it T(A,B) = S P (A⊗B) P^T S. The same table is written alongside in Latin letters for C = [[a,b],[c,∂]] and D = [[a1,b1],[c1,∂1]]: aa1, -bb1, ba1, ab1 / -cc1, ∂∂1, -∂c1, -c∂1 / ca1, -∂b1, ∂a1, cb1 / ac1, -b∂1, bc1, a∂1.

(C) Composing two composites. Riemann forms row 1 of T(A,B) times column 1 of T(C,D):
αα1·aa1 + ββ1·cc1 + βα1·ca1 + αβ1·ac1 = (αa+βc)(α1a1+β1c1).
This equals (AC)_11·(BD)_11, i.e. the corresponding entry of T(AC,BD). This is the mixed-product rule (A⊗B)(C⊗D) = AC⊗BD, i.e. composition of 4-variable substitutions corresponds to composition of the two binary factors separately. Next to it is the expression (αa+βc)(α1a1+β1c1) - (a1b1+β1∂1)(ab+β∂). It mixes Greek and Latin letters and looks like an attempt at a 2x2 minor of the product; its intent is unclear.

(D) The table '22'. The rows (1, -βγ, β, γ) are multiplied against (1, -α2α3, α2, α3), alongside an index grid 11…44. This is an outer product of two vectors of the same 'decomposable' type, i.e. the Kronecker product applied to rank-one data. The subscripts are written loosely.

(E) Primed letters. A substitution with entries that are products of one of (a, c, a', c') and one of (b, ∂, b', ∂') is considered, e.g. x1 = ab x1 - a∂ x2 + a'b x3 + a∂' x4 (sign/primes partly uncertain), and another y1 = -c'b x1 + …. This is again a Kronecker-type product, of [[a,a'],[c,c']] with a matrix in b, ∂, b', ∂'. Riemann computes
-ab·c'b' - a'∂·c∂' + a'b·cb' + a∂·c'∂' = (a'c - ac')(bb' - ∂∂').
This is a 2x2 minor (compound) of the Kronecker-type substitution factoring as the product of the two binary determinants.

Purpose (my interpretation): Riemann is verifying that the 4-variable substitutions of this special shape form a closed family under composition, parametrised by pairs of binary substitutions. Their determinants and minors factor through the binary determinants. In modern terms this is the homomorphism GL2×GL2 → GL4, (A,B) ↦ A⊗B. That homomorphism underlies SL2×SL2 → SO(2,2) (or SU2×SU2 → SO4, i.e. Cayley's quaternion description of 4D rotations), via X ↦ A X B^T on 2x2 matrices X. The application is not stated on the page.
errors: In the explicit composed expressions the fourth line reads α(γ1x1+δ1x4)+β(+δ1x2 ± γ1x3), with visibly altered signs. Taken with the inner row δ1x2-γ1x3 used in line 2, it would give the x2 coefficient +βδ1, inconsistent with the final table entry -βδ1. The final table (αγ1, -βδ1, βγ1, αδ1) is the correct one for a consistent signed Kronecker pattern, so the slip was corrected in the table.

The expression (αa+βc)(α1a1+β1c1) - (a1b1+β1∂1)(ab+β∂) mixes letters in a way that does not correspond to a clean minor of T(A,B)T(C,D) (e.g. 'ab' where 'αb' would be expected). It is probably an unfinished or miscopied attempt.
In the primed-letter tables some primes and signs are inconsistent between the x- and y-substitutions. The identity only works with the last term a∂c'∂' (primed ∂'), not a∂c'∂.
The top fraction array cannot be checked fully. It seems to have some entries missing a factor (e.g. -(c2/a2)(∂1/b) has mismatched indices), probably index slips.

results.what: Composition of two 4-variable substitutions of the special form gives coefficients that are products of entries of two binary substitutions, i.e. a signed-permuted Kronecker product A⊗B.
results.modern_name: Kronecker (tensor) product of matrices; homomorphism GL2×GL2→GL4 (cf. SL2×SL2→SO(2,2), SU2×SU2→SO(4))
results.usually_credited_to: Zehfuss (1858, determinant of the product); Kronecker (lectures, 1860s–80s); Hurwitz 1894; Cayley 1855 for 4D rotations as pairs of quaternion multiplications

results.what: Entry of the product of two such composites factors: αα1aa1+ββ1cc1+βα1ca1+αβ1ac1 = (αa+βc)(α1a1+β1c1), i.e. T(A,B)T(C,D)=T(AC,BD).
results.usually_credited_to: folklore of 19th-century invariant theory; explicit in Hurwitz (1894), Kronecker

results.what: A 2x2 minor of a Kronecker-type substitution equals the product of the binary determinants: -ab c'b' - a'∂ c∂' + a'b cb' + a∂ c'∂' = (a'c-ac')(bb'-∂∂').
results.modern_name: Compound/minor of a tensor product; Zehfuss determinant identity det(A⊗B)=det(A)^2 det(B)^2 (for 2x2)

results.what: The special 4x4 substitution M splits into two 2x2 blocks with the same determinant, so det M = -(αδ-βγ)^2 (my computation; not written on the page).
results.modern_name: block decomposition / determinant of a permuted block-diagonal matrix

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine 19th-century algebra of linear substitutions. Riemann checks that 4-variable substitutions of a special form compose like pairs of binary substitutions (a signed Kronecker product with the mixed-product rule), and that a minor factors into binary determinants. This was in the air: Cayley 1855 on 4D rotations, Zehfuss 1858. It is a mildly interesting unpublished trace of Riemann working with what amounts to the SL2×SL2 → SO(2,2)/SO(4) correspondence. There is no new theorem, and the purpose (possibly quaternions, conformal or line geometry) is not recorded.
